# v0.1.0 — initial release

An unofficial Home Assistant integration for MENNEKES AMTRON wallboxes over
local Modbus RTU. Built against the manufacturer's Modbus RTU specification
revision 2.5, register layout v01.03, and developed for an AMTRON 4You 310
11 C2.

> **Not yet verified on hardware.** Everything here comes from the
> specification and is exercised against a real Modbus RTU server over a
> virtual serial link, but none of it has been measured on a real wallbox.
> Start in read-only mode and work through
> [docs/quickstart.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md).

## Why not the built-in `modbus:` integration

Because `0x0302` is not a charging-current limit. It is three commands sharing
one register:

| Written | What the wallbox does |
|---|---|
| `0` | **No limitation** — signals its *maximum* current |
| `0.01`–`5.99` | Invalid — signals 0 A, the documented way to pause |
| `≥ 6` | A real limit |

A YAML `number` with `min: 0` therefore requests **full load** when somebody
drags the slider to zero. Here the slider cannot go below 6 A, pausing has its
own switch, and "no limitation" needs an explicit opt-in on an action.

The heartbeat is the same kind of problem: `0x0D00 = 0x55AA` has to arrive
every ten seconds or the wallbox stops charging. It runs in its own task, so a
slow poll can never starve it.

## What you get

- **Setup that finds the wallbox.** The form reads the device before creating
  an entry, and searches the bus when the address or the bus parameters are
  not the factory ones.
- **A read-only first run.** New entries never write and send no heartbeat.
- **36 sensors, 9 binary sensors and 8 controls**, in English and German,
  gated by what the firmware and the hardware actually support.
- **Four blueprints**, installed with the integration: PV surplus charging,
  pause and resume with hysteresis, heartbeat recovery, §14a notification.
- **§14a visibility.** The grid-operator downgrade is enforced in the wallbox;
  this makes it visible and never works around it.
- **Diagnostics** with the full raw register image, no port path and a hashed
  serial number, plus four repair issues for the four ways this device gets
  stuck.

## Install

HACS → custom repository → category *Integration*, or download
`ha-mennekes-amtron-manual.zip` and unpack it over your configuration
directory. Hardware wiring and DIP switches are in
[docs/hardware.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/main/docs/hardware.md);
read
[docs/safety.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/main/docs/safety.md)
before enabling control.

## Assets

`ha-mennekes-amtron.zip` is the HACS asset and has no wrapping folder.
`ha-mennekes-amtron-manual.zip` carries the full
`custom_components/mennekes_amtron/` path for manual installation.
`SHA256SUMS`, `build-metadata.json` and an SPDX SBOM accompany them; the zip
build is reproducible from the recorded commit.
